title: Responsive Design and Media Queries
description: Master mobile-first responsive web design: configure viewport meta tags, write @media queries, define breakpoint strategy, and adapt Flexbox/Grid layouts across devices.

objectives.statement: Configure viewport meta tags and write mobile-first CSS @media queries using min-width breakpoints.
Adapt multi-column layouts into single-column mobile structures dynamically across breakpoints.

content.title: Mobile-First Responsive Engineering
content.hook: Today's web users browse on everything from 320px wristwatch screens to 4K desktop displays. Building responsive UIs ensures seamless accessibility on every device.
content.context: Responsive design rests on three pillars: 1. Viewport meta tag (`<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`), 2. Fluid layout tracks, 3. Mobile-first `@media (min-width: 768px)` queries that progressively enhance layouts on larger viewports.
goals: Include the essential Viewport meta tag in HTML `<head>`.
Transform single-column mobile layouts into multi-column desktop grids.
Avoid anti-patterns like hardcoded `max-width` queries that pollute base CSS.

content.title: Mobile-First Progressive Enhancement
content.description: Base Styles (0px+): 1-column layout for phones → @media (min-width: 640px): 2-column layout for tablets → @media (min-width: 1024px): 3-column layout for desktop.

content.prompt: Look at the mobile-first CSS below. On a device screen width of 800px, what is the background color of `.card`?
options: transparent (media queries override base styles completely)

feedback.correct: Spot on! 800px satisfies `min-width: 640px` (so `lightblue` applies) but does NOT satisfy `min-width: 1024px`. The card displays lightblue.
feedback.incorrect: Evaluate `min-width` conditions: 800px is greater than or equal to 640px (matches), but less than 1024px (does not match). Thus, lightblue wins.

content.title: Build a Responsive Mobile-First Feature Grid
content.prompt:
Write mobile-first CSS for `.feature-grid`:
1. Base styles (mobile): Set `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 1rem;`.
2. Write a media query `@media (min-width: 768px)` that expands `.feature-grid` to 3 columns: `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr)` and `gap: 1.5rem`.
3. Style `.feature` with `padding: 1.5rem; background: #ffffff; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #e2e8f0;`.
content.starterCode:
Fast Execution

Sub-millisecond compilation speed.

Type Safe

Full schema validation out of the box.

Accessible

Built with WCAG AAA standards in mind.

testCases.description: .feature must have padding and background color

feedback.correct: Masterful responsive design! Mobile users get a crisp 1-column stack, while tablet and desktop viewports automatically scale to 3 columns via min-width media queries.
feedback.incorrect: Review your code: define `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr; gap: 1rem;` on base `.feature-grid`, and override to `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);` inside `@media (min-width: 768px)`.

content.prompt: Why is a mobile-first approach (using `min-width` media queries) preferred over desktop-first (using `max-width` queries) in modern frontend engineering?

feedback.correct: Great analysis! Mobile-first architecture writes simpler, lighter base CSS for mobile devices (which have less processing power) and progressively layer complex grid/flex rules on larger screens, preventing CSS override bloat.
feedback.incorrect: Think about code complexity, performance on mobile hardware, and progressive enhancement versus desktop degradation.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Responsive Web Design
takeaways: The viewport meta tag scales HTML pages to match device width without artificial zoom.
Mobile-first CSS writes default styles for small screens and uses min-width queries for larger displays.
Combine fluid units (%, fr, rem) with CSS Grid/Flexbox for seamless multi-device adaptation.
